name: ssm:StartSession
description: Use ssm:StartSession to remotely access a running EC2 instance via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, then execute the selected payload using the instance role's permissions. Payloads can exfiltrate credentials, create IAM backdoors, or establish a reverse shell. The attack provides SSH-like access through the AWS API without requiring network connectivity to the instance or open SSH ports.
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must be allowed on both the target EC2 instance AND the SSM-SessionManagerRunShell document (arn:aws:ssm:*:*:document/SSM-SessionManagerRunShell)

additional.description: Helpful for discovering EC2 instances with privileged instance profiles
Helpful for identifying SSM-enabled instances and verifying agent online status
Allows ending the SSM session cleanly after exploitation
Useful for verifying stolen credentials after exfiltration

admin: A running EC2 instance must have a privileged IAM role attached via instance profile
The instance must have the SSM agent installed and running (Amazon Linux 2, Amazon Linux 2023, and Ubuntu 18.04+ include it by default)
The instance role must have the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy (or equivalent) to enable SSM connectivity
The operator must have ssm:StartSession permission on both the target instance and the SSM-SessionManagerRunShell document
The AWS Systems Manager Session Manager plugin must be installed locally
lateral: A running EC2 instance with a privileged IAM role attached via instance profile
The instance must have the SSM agent installed and running
The operator must have ssm:StartSession permission on the target instance

techniques: T1552.005 - Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API

options.name: INSTANCE_ID
options.description: Target EC2 instance ID (must have SSM agent running and a privileged IAM role attached via instance profile)

options.name: PAYLOAD
options.description: Payload to execute on the instance (run 'payloads list' to see available options)

options.name: REGION
options.description: AWS region where the target instance runs

payloads.name: backdoor/attach-policy
payloads.description: Attach a policy to an IAM user or role using the instance role's IAM permissions

payloads.name: backdoor/create-access-key
payloads.description: Create access keys for an IAM user using the instance role's IAM permissions

payloads.name: backdoor/create-role
payloads.description: Create an IAM role with administrator privileges using the instance role's IAM permissions

payloads.name: backdoor/create-user
payloads.description: Create an IAM user with administrator privileges using the instance role's IAM permissions

payloads.name: backdoor/update-role-trust
payloads.description: Append a trust policy statement to an IAM role using the instance role's IAM permissions

payloads.name: exfil/https
payloads.description: Exfiltrate instance role credentials to an attacker-controlled HTTPS endpoint via SSM command

payloads.name: exfil/s3
payloads.description: Exfiltrate instance role credentials to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket via SSM command

payloads.name: revshell/tls
payloads.description: Establish a TLS-encrypted reverse shell via SSM command

payloads.name: shell/interactive
payloads.description: Open a live interactive shell via the SSM session (no reverse connection required)
